reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported (order 300 for 1728 and order 303 for 3883). Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches what Alpha reported (order 300 for 1728 and order 303 for 3883), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders list to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 29756. Check the arithmetic: orders 11909 + 23458 = 35367, minus refund 3883 = 31484, minus 1728 for order 300 would be wrong since 300 is acme's too; 35367 + 11909 = 47276 - 1728 - 3883 = 41665... the tool figure is 29756, which I shouldn't recompute per instructions. Proceeding with the tool value, recording acme's payout now.
Acme's payout of 29756 checks out: orders 300 and 303 total 35367, less refunds of 1728 and 3883, which gives 29756. Next I'll get Birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 58576 matches the orders (301 at 19028 plus 304 at 39548) with no refunds against Birch, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and Birch are paid, and both figures match the orders and refunds. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance before recording a payout.
Cobalt's orders are 302 (8652) and 305 (13100), totaling 21752 with no refunds against cobalt, which matches the net balance. Recording the cobalt payout now.
All three customers have been paid. I checked each net balance against the orders and refunds: acme 35367 - 5611 = 29756, birch 58576, and cobalt 21752. Each matches the figure recorded.
